title: Literature 2015-2026: no surviving sub-sqrt claim; m>=4 decomposition finder is the only open index-calculus route
question: Literature survey (ECDLP-58, 2015-2026, sources and read levels in experiments/round17-literature/survey.md): no surviving claim of a sub-sqrt(p) algorithm for generic prime-order prime-field curves; Semaev 2015 subexponential claim is binary-field and FFDA-dependent (FFDA doubted, char-2 counterexamples by Huang-Kosters-Yeo and Kosters-Yeo 2015); Petit-Kosters-Messeng 2016 prime-field algorithm outperformed by generic methods at practical sizes; Corrigan-Gibbs-Kogan S T^2 bound tight generically, Dinur-Keller-Marmor add non-adaptive preprocessing bound; the only ML "break" found is an unvetted preprint. Untested routes all have priors <= ~1% (dedicated non-Groebner finder at m=4,5; Mahalanobis-Mallick Problem L; isogeny distance to structured curves).
rationale: Unused 10% literature allocation; checks that the lab is not missing published progress.
claims: Literature survey (ECDLP-58, 2015-2026, sources and read levels in experiments/round17-literature/survey.md): no surviving claim of a sub-sqrt(p) algorithm for generic prime-order prime-field curves; Semaev 2015 subexponential claim is binary-field and FFDA-dependent (FFDA doubted, char-2 counterexamples by Huang-Kosters-Yeo and Kosters-Yeo 2015); Petit-Kosters-Messeng 2016 prime-field algorithm outperformed by generic methods at practical sizes; Corrigan-Gibbs-Kogan S T^2 bound tight generically, Dinur-Keller-Marmor add non-adaptive preprocessing bound; the only ML "break" found is an unvetted preprint. Untested routes all have priors <= ~1% (dedicated non-Groebner finder at m=4,5; Mahalanobis-Mallick Problem L; isogeny distance to structured curves).

PI derivation (unreviewed), answering the survey caveat that inventor E/F supply bounds count only base-closed relations whereas PKM-style relations use randomised targets R=aP+bQ with unlimited supply: a random target decomposes over a base of size s into m points with probability ~ s^m/p (up to m!), about s relations are needed, so total cost >= (p/s^{m-1}) * T_test + LA(s). m=2: max(p/s, s) >= sqrt p even with free finder and linear-time linear algebra (inventor E conclusion stands). m=3 with LA ~ s^2: p/s^2 + s^2 >= sqrt p (tie at best; consistent with inventor F and PKM). m>=4: s = p^{1/(m+1)} would give p^{2/(m+1)} < sqrt p only if the per-target decomposition test costs T_test < p^{1/2 - 2/(m+1)} (m=4: < p^{1/10} at s = p^{1/5}), whereas generic list-merge costs ~ s^{m/2} = p^{2/5}. The m>=4 finder question is the only index-calculus route left open.
